stubs.how: Node http server .ui-capture/stub/server.js serving /api/v1/* from db.json (generated by .ui-capture/stub/seed.js). It runs in-process inside .ui-capture/front.js on a free loopback port; front.js listens on PORT (4486) and routes /api/v1/* and /ghost/* to it, everything else to `next start` (also on a free internal port). NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:4486/api/v1 (set in .env.local, baked at build). Write endpoints (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) accept and echo the payload.

Stub returns Keycloak-shaped JWT access/refresh tokens for the seeded user (realm roles include view-supporters + view-contact-requests, so the admin panel is also accessible). Sign in with the real /login form via next-auth credentials provider.
GOOGLE_ID/GOOGLE_SECRET are placeholders; use email/password login instead.

stubs.service: File storage (S3) for campaign / news / blog images
stubs.how: Stub renders category-themed landscape illustrations (SVG -> JPEG via sharp, cached in .ui-capture/stub/img-cache) for /campaign-file/:id, /campaign-news-file/:id and blog feature images.
GHOST_API_URL=http://localhost:4486/ghost; the stub answers /ghost/api/content/posts and /posts/slug/:slug with 12 seeded posts.
Placeholder publishable keys; /stripe/prices* are served by the stub, payment-intent/setup-intent POSTs are echoed. No real checkout is possible offline.

next/font/google is fed by NEXT_FONT_GOOGLE_MOCKED_RESPONSES=.ui-capture/tools/google-fonts-mock.js, which points at the real Commissioner/Montserrat variable fonts from @fontsource-variable npm packages.
No DSN configured (Sentry dry-run in development APP_ENV); GTM only loads after cookie consent and simply fails offline.

app.notes: Podkrepi.bg (Bulgarian donation platform) frontend, Next.js 14 production build (`next build`, node 24.11.1 + yarn 3.3.0 via mise) run with `next start` on PORT. start.sh runs .ui-capture/front.js, the only process that binds a fixed port (PORT=4486); it hosts the stub API in-process and starts the Next server on a free internal port, proxying to both. Data (deterministic, regenerated by `node .ui-capture/stub/seed.js`): 38 campaigns in Bulgarian across 14 campaign types (active, complete, partially financed, paused, suspended, blocked, draft), ~2,350 donations/payments spread over ~2.5 years in EUR with mixed statuses (succeeded, refund, declined, waiting...), 280+ donor wishes, 55 campaign news articles, 78 expenses, 38 recurring donations, 18 withdrawals, 8 transfers, 160 bank transactions, 161 people, 10 companies, 12 campaign applications, support/contact requests, irregularity reports, documents, bank accounts, 12 blog posts. Signed-in user Десислава Маринова (member since March 2023) has 50+ donations including monthly recurring gifts, organizes 4 campaigns, follows 6 campaigns, and has a pending campaign application. Main areas: home (/), campaigns list (/campaigns) and campaign pages (/campaigns/<slug>, with donations, wishes, news, expenses, statistics), campaign news (/campaigns/news), blog (/blog), profile (/profile/donations, /profile/recurring-donations, /profile/my-campaigns, /profile/my-notifications, /profile/personal-information, /profile/certificates), admin panel (/admin: campaigns, donations, payments, bank transactions, persons, vaults, withdrawals, expenses, campaign applications, etc.). Default locale is Bulgarian; /en/... for English. Build note: yarn install needed a local CONNECT relay (.ui-capture/tools/proxy-relay.js) for the sandbox proxy and removal of .idea/.vscode folders from three cached package zips (sandbox write restriction); no source files were changed.

# Running it
- Follow the repo's own setup docs and tooling. Take the simplest route that shows the real app: a static production build if the front end works without a backend, otherwise the app's own server (production or dev mode).
- If it needs a database or other services, run them locally with an embedded or file-based option (SQLite, in-memory, JSON files, an embedded Postgres such as PGlite) or the app's demo/mock mode.
- Don't redesign or restyle anything. Change only what's needed to build and run it.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):
- Give the required variables placeholder values so the app starts.
- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). Docker isn't available. A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4486 (e.g. 5486) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4486 is stopped before I check.

# When you're done, leave this in ./.ui-capture/
- app.json: {"mode": "static" or "server", "entry": "/path where the main UI opens", "login": null or {"username": "...", "email": "...", "password": "..."}, "stubs": [{"service": "what was faked", "how": "how"}], "notes": "how you set it up, what data is loaded, and the main areas of the app"}
- static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4486/ (it gets PORT=4486). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

# Order of work
You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
1. Get the app building and running with its stubs, and write the contract above (app.json plus out/ or start.sh), even if it has only a little data so far.
2. Then build out the data, re-running your seed and checking the app still loads after each substantial step, so that a working state with the data loaded so far is always in place.
Write large data sets with a short generator script rather than as one long literal file.
